name: Salt
oneLine: Charged atoms dissolved in the water, like sodium and chloride.
howItWorks: Salt splits into charged atoms in water. They crowd around anything with an opposite charge. Too much salt pulls water out of bubbles and cells.
deeper: Early oceans and pools were salty, but by how much is debated. Some fatty-acid bubbles fall apart in seawater-level salt, one reason warm freshwater pools are a popular setting.
sizeComparison: a 500,000th the width of a hair
simplification: Ions are drawn as dots. Colours are not real.
